model_claims.text: isoparse now accepts hour-only UTC offsets (+05, -05).
On master, hour-only offset strings are silently parsed as fractional time because the regex requires at least four offset digits.
model_claims.source_quote: _ISO_TZ_RE required at least four offset digits, so `'+05'` never matched as a timezone suffix, stayed in the string body, and was then **silently parsed as fractional time**: `'2026-11-09T12:00:00+05'` → `12:00:00.050000` (and `datetime.fromisoformat` parses the same string as `12:00:00+05:00`).

model_claims.text: On master, an hour-only offset with a fractional second causes a TypeError during parsing.
model_claims.source_quote: With a fractional second present it didn't stay silent: `'...12:00:00.5+05'` raised `TypeError: argument for function given by name ('tzinfo') and position (8)`.

model_claims.text: After the fix, all previously supported ISO‑8601 offset suffixes remain unchanged.
model_claims.source_quote: The fix accepts a two-digit offset in the regex and treats missing minutes as zero (`int(digits[2:4] or 0)`, same pattern the seconds already used). All previously supported suffix shapes (`Z`, `±HH:MM`, `±HHMM`, `±HH:MM:SS`, `±HH:MM:SS.f`) are unchanged, including the `+25:00` rejection test.

model_claims.text: The new test for hour‑only offsets fails on master but passes with the patch.
model_claims.source_quote: New `test_isoparse_hour_only_offset` fails on `master` (d31d821), passes with this patch:

model_claims.text: Running the full test suite with the patch shows no existing tests or doctests altered.
model_claims.source_quote: Full suite with the patch: `622 passed, 22 subtests passed` — no existing test or doctest changed.
